key_insight: In laser-TIG hybrid welding of Invar steel, higher laser power and welding current deepen and widen the molten pool, while higher travel speed reduces heat input, penetration, and weld width; arc behavior becomes more unstable or deflected at higher power/speed.
engineering_relevance: These process–fluidity relationships provide practical guidance for tuning hybrid welding parameters to improve weld geometry and arc stability in low-expansion Invar steel applications.
method: High-speed photography of arc and pool behavior
Parameter sweep over laser power, welding speed, and current
evidence_signal: The abstract reports comparative simulation and high-speed imaging results across laser power (5–6 kW), welding speed (0.5–0.8 m/min), and current (150–170 A), linking each setting to changes in penetration, weld width, flow, and arc shape.
watch_item: The findings are parameter-window specific, so transfer to different joint geometries, shielding conditions, or machine setups should be validated experimentally before production use.
paper_title: Molten pool dynamic behavior and arc characteristics in laser-TIG hybrid welding of Invar steel
